Part Description: 
As part of the planned inspection scope, CT1 was given a thorough inspection, conducted by 
GE personnel. The scope included turbine, compressor, lift oil lines, and combustion 
components. A list of TIL's were also addressed during this inspection. The list of TIL's are 
included in the attached broescope inspection report for this outage. 
Recommendation Status: Should be planned for next Outage
Recommendation Type: Services
Recommendation Description: 
It is recommended that regular borescopes be conducted on all components of this unit, 
following GE guidelines. No findings from this report would necessitate a change to the 
planned schedule.

Foreword 
 
This report describes and documents the borescope inspection of the turbine described in the Site and 
Unit Information section with respect to normal wear, rubs, fouling, depositing, oxidation, erosion, 
spallation, cracking, missing material, foreign object damage and other abnormal conditions. 
 
Color images depicting the condition of the turbine were captured using the Waygate technologies’ 
Mentor Visual iQ Videoscope System with a 4.5m X 6.1mm flexible probe.  The interior of the turbine was 
illuminated using an external light source. 
 
The images included in the photo report show typical, and/or abnormal, conditions of the components 
observed for documentation and comparison during future inspections.  It is important to note that due 
to the magnification of the lens, object viewed through the videoscope may be significantly magnified.  It 
is also important to note that videoscopes have certain minor imperfections inherent in their 
construction, caused by lens distortion.  As a result, a surface, which is straight or true, may seem to 
appear slightly curved in a photograph.  This is no problem for the inspector since multiple views and 
close-ups easily yield the actual condition of the area.  However, due to the possibility of optical 
distortion, judgments concerning any section of component of the turbine are best made at the time of 
the examination.  Interpretation of the photographs should be made by someone familiar with 
videoscope photography. 
 
 
Unit Access 
 
Access to the compressor section was possible through the Bellmouth were the IGVs and the first fourteen 
rotating stages.  
Access to the combustion section was possible by entering through the removed DLNs con cans 1, 2, 6, 7, 8, 
12, 13, 14. 
Access to the turbine section was possible through the BI ports for each stage located on the top of the unit.  
Additional access to S1N and S1B was possible through the DLN on can 12.

Observations 
 
Peripherals 
 
Not inspected. The plugs not being able to be removed 
 
Compressor Section 
 
All the compressor show evidence of deposits and oxidation/corrosion in stage 8 to 14. 
 
The R4 blades that were examined show tip curl. 
 
The R5 blades that were examined show minor LE FOD impacts on a one blade. 
 
The R8 blades that were examined show minor LE FOD impacts on a couple of blades. 
 
The R9 blades that were examined show minor LE FOD impacts on a one blade. 
 
The R12 blades that were examined show minor LE FOD impacts on a one blade.  
 
The R13 blades that were examined show lower case rub and tip curl. 
 
The R14 blades that were examined show lower case rub.   
 
The S14 vanes that were examined show tip curl on the vanes at the six o’clock position.  Rotor rub was 
also observed.   
 
Stages 15-17 blades and vanes were not inspected due to all 6 CDC plugs not being able to be removed. 
 
Combustion Section 
 
All 14 effusion plates show deposits and oxidation/erosion. 
 
The effusion plates in cans 1, 5, 8 each show 1 crack.  Cans 6, 11, 13 and 14 each show 2 cracks. 
 
The PM3 in can 11 show evidence of what appear to be burning/erosion. 
 
Turbine Section 
 
The S1N that were examined show Pressure Side chordal cracks on numerous vanes. Inner Sidewall 
oxidation/erosion was observed at several segment joints.  Additionally, Outer Sidewall relief radius 
cracks were observed. Inner Sidewall and Outer Sidewall TBC spallation and cracks were also observed.   
 
Page 11 of 608

GE Power 
 
Inspection & Life Extension Services 
 
Page 8 of 126 
The S1B that were examined show LE Suction Side TBC spallation. Rub was also observed on the LE of 
the blade platforms. Additionally, TBC spallation and wear was observed on the blade tips.   
 
The S1S that was examined show TBC spallation as well as oxidation/erosion.  
 
The S2N that were examined show LE PS chordal cracks. TE cracks were also observed.  
Additionally, Inner Sidewall relief radius cracks were observed. 
  
The S2B that were examined show oxidation/erosion on the outer side of the blade shroud tips.  
 
The S2S honeycomb that was examined show in good condition. 
 
The S3N that were examined show LE Pressure Side deposits.   
 
The S3B that were examined show LE blend repairs.  
 
The S3S honeycomb that was examined show in good condition.

Foreword 
 
This report describes and documents the borescope inspection of the turbine described in the Site and Unit 
Information section with respect to normal wear, rubs, fouling, depositing, oxidation, erosion, spallation, 
cracking, missing material, foreign object damage and other abnormal conditions. 
 
Color images depicting the condition of the turbine were captured using the Waygate technologies’ Mentor 
Visual iQ Videoscope System with a 4.5m X 6.1mm flexible probe.  The interior of the turbine was 
illuminated using an external light source. 
 
The images included in the photo report show typical, and/or abnormal, conditions of the components 
observed for documentation and comparison during future inspections.  It is important to note that due to 
the magnification of the lens, object viewed through the videoscope may be significantly magnified.  It is 
also important to note that videoscopes have certain minor imperfections inherent in their construction, 
caused by lens distortion.  As a result, a surface, which is straight or true, may seem to appear slightly 
curved in a photograph.  This is no problem for the inspector since multiple views and close-ups easily 
yield the actual condition of the area.  However, due to the possibility of optical distortion, judgments 
concerning any section of component of the turbine are best made at the time of the examination.  
Interpretation of the photographs should be made by someone familiar with videoscope photography. 
 
 
Unit Access 
 
Access to the number one bearing lift oil lines was gained by entering the removal of the right plug 
located in the load compartment area.  Access to the compressor was gained through the inlet plenum 
where the inlet guide vanes and the first fourteen rotating and stationary stages were examined.  Access 
to the combustion components was gained by entering through the DLN port located in combustion cans 
one, two, twelve, six, seven, eight, and fourteen.  Borescope ports in the turbine casing allowed viewing of 
the first stage nozzle, first stage buckets, second stage nozzle, second stage buckets, third stage nozzle, 
and third stage buckets.

Foreword 
 
This report describes and documents the borescope inspection of the turbine described in the Site and Unit 
Information section with respect to normal wear, rubs, fouling, depositing, oxidation, erosion, spallation, 
cracking, missing material, foreign object damage and other abnormal conditions. 
 
Color images depicting the condition of the turbine were captured using the Waygate technologies’ Mentor 
Visual iQ Videoscope System with a 4.5m X 6.1mm flexible probe.  The interior of the turbine was illuminated 
using an external light source. 
 
The images included in the photo report show typical, and/or abnormal, conditions of the components observed 
for documentation and comparison during future inspections.  It is important to note that due to the 
magnification of the lens, object viewed through the videoscope may be significantly magnified.  It is also 
important to note that videoscopes have certain minor imperfections inherent in their construction, caused by 
lens distortion.  As a result, a surface, which is straight or true, may seem to appear slightly curved in a 
photograph.  This is no problem for the inspector since multiple views and close-ups easily yield the actual 
condition of the area.  However, due to the possibility of optical distortion, judgments concerning any section 
of component of the turbine are best made at the time of the examination.  Interpretation of the photographs 
should be made by someone familiar with videoscope photography. 
 
 
Unit Access 
 
Access to the compressor was gained through the inlet plenum where the inlet guide vanes and the first 
fourteen rotating and stationary stages were examined.  Access to the combustion components was gained by 
entering through the DLN port located in combustion cans one, two, twelve, seven and fourteen.  Borescope 
ports in the turbine casing allowed viewing of the first stage nozzle, first stage buckets, second stage nozzle, 
second stage buckets, third stage nozzle, and third stage buckets.

Foreword 
 
This report describes and documents the borescope inspection of the turbine described in the Site and Unit 
Information section with respect to normal wear, rubs, fouling, depositing, oxidation, erosion, spallation, 
cracking, missing material, foreign object damage and other abnormal conditions. 
 
Color images depicting the condition of the turbine were captured using the Waygate technologies’ Mentor 
Visual iQ Videoscope System with a 4.5m X 6.1mm flexible probe.  The interior of the turbine was illuminated 
using an external light source. 
 
The images included in the photo report show typical, and/or abnormal, conditions of the components observed 
for documentation and comparison during future inspections.  It is important to note that due to the 
magnification of the lens, object viewed through the videoscope may be significantly magnified.  It is also 
important to note that videoscopes have certain minor imperfections inherent in their construction, caused by 
lens distortion.  As a result, a surface, which is straight or true, may seem to appear slightly curved in a 
photograph.  This is no problem for the inspector since multiple views and close-ups easily yield the actual 
condition of the area.  However, due to the possibility of optical distortion, judgments concerning any section 
of component of the turbine are best made at the time of the examination.  Interpretation of the photographs 
should be made by someone familiar with videoscope photography. 
 
 
Unit Access 
 
Access to the compressor was gained through the inlet plenum where the inlet guide vanes and the first 
fourteen rotating and stationary stages were examined.  Access to the combustion components was gained by 
entering through the DLN port located in combustion cans one, two, twelve, seven and fourteen.  Borescope 
ports in the turbine casing allowed viewing of the first stage nozzle, first stage buckets, second stage nozzle, 
second stage buckets, third stage nozzle, and third stage buckets.

Foreword 
 
This report describes and documents the borescope inspection of the turbine described in the Site and Unit 
Information section with respect to normal wear, rubs, fouling, depositing, oxidation, erosion, spallation, 
cracking, missing material, foreign object damage and other abnormal conditions. 
 
Color images depicting the condition of the turbine were captured using the Waygate technologies’ Mentor 
Visual iQ Videoscope System with a 4.5m X 6.1mm flexible probe.  The interior of the turbine was illuminated 
using an external light source. 
 
The images included in the photo report show typical, and/or abnormal, conditions of the components observed 
for documentation and comparison during future inspections.  It is important to note that due to the 
magnification of the lens, object viewed through the videoscope may be significantly magnified.  It is also 
important to note that videoscopes have certain minor imperfections inherent in their construction, caused by 
lens distortion.  As a result, a surface, which is straight or true, may seem to appear slightly curved in a 
photograph.  This is no problem for the inspector since multiple views and close-ups easily yield the actual 
condition of the area.  However, due to the possibility of optical distortion, judgments concerning any section 
of component of the turbine are best made at the time of the examination.  Interpretation of the photographs 
should be made by someone familiar with videoscope photography. 
 
 
Unit Access 
 
Access to the compressor was gained through the inlet plenum where the inlet guide vanes and the first 
fourteen rotating and stationary stages were examined.  Access to the combustion components was gained by 
entering through the DLN port located in combustion cans one, two, twelve, seven and fourteen.  Borescope 
ports in the turbine casing allowed viewing of the first stage nozzle, first stage buckets, second stage nozzle, 
second stage buckets, third stage nozzle, and third stage buckets.

Observations 
 
Peripherals 
 
Not inspected. The plugs not being able to be removed. 
 
Compressor Section 
 
All the compressor show evidence of deposits. 
 
The shims in the right-side show evidence of separation between them. 
 
The R1 blades that were examined show evidence LE PS FOD impact on one particular blade. 
 
The S9 vanes that were examined show rubbing in the rotor. 
 
Starting the R9 – R14, show evidence of corrosion/oxidation and deposits. 
 
The R12, R13, R14 blades that were examined show evidence minor LE PS FOD impact on blades. 
 
Stages 15-17 blades and vanes were not inspected due to all 6 CDC plugs not being able to be removed. 
 
Combustion Section 
 
The effusion plates show minor oxidation and deposits in all cans. 
 
The effusion plate in can 10 show evidence of one crack. 
 
The Flame Detector in can 11 show evidence of burning and misalignment. 
 
The Flame Detector in can 12 show evidence of misalignment. 
 
The CDM in can 1, can 3, can 4, can 5, can 6, can 8, can 9 show misalignments.
